_numbering_note: catalog_number pending the base/hybrid renumbering (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md); csv_id is the authoritative key for now.
sub_palette: old_persian (axsatran) backbone + latinate (agrippan) substrate (cross-family blend, Persian-leaning)

blend.backbone: old_persian (axsatran: the satrapal court and the King of Kings, the Old-Persian flowing vowels a/i/u with long a/i/u, the spirants th/x/f, the ezafe genitive-of-relation '-ahya', the horse-element -aspa and the glory-element -farnah, the cardinal virtue Arta against the Lie Drauga, SOV with heavy-syllable stress, the paridaida garden and the apadana hall)
blend.substrate: latinate (agrippan: the Roman civic spine - the via and iter roads, the castra forts and the urbs cities, the legio and the forum, the law-stele and the tribute-roll, the -us/-um/-a endings and penultimate stress, the legal and engineering register of a road-and-law empire)
blend.lean: Persian-heavy - Ctesiphon and Rome made one crown: a Perso-Roman empire where the Old-Persian court is the spine. Its rule, kin, court and land register endure, the throne is the Shah, the King of Kings - while the conquered-and-wedded Roman west lends the civic, legal, road and material vocabulary, the Imperator-style imperial title, and the engineering of a law-and-road state. A Sassanid-Byzantine synthesis: the eternal rivals fused into a single crowned law-and-court.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_04 (Persian/Axsatran) x BASE_06 (Roman/Agrippan). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Persian base = Civilized and Roman base = Civilized, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Romaria is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a Perso-Roman empire - Ctesiphon and Rome as one, the eternal rivals fused into a single crowned law-and-court (a Sassanid-Byzantine synthesis). Backbone/lean = Old Persian (the satrapal court, the King of Kings, the rule/kin/court/land register, the Arta/Drauga moral frame); substrate = Latinate Roman (the civic/legal/road/material vocabulary, the imperial title, the engineering register). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Old-Persian register (allowed, catalog 5.3); the kingdom-tier display ruler is the approved foreign term 'Shah' (the Persian throne) and the empire-tier display ruler is the approved foreign term 'Imperator' (the Roman imperial style) - both recorded in approved_foreign_terms_used. DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Old-Persian-shifted reflexes PRIMARY, Latinate Agrippan morphs SECONDARY), never real Iranian/Roman gods. All three alignments (standard lens). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are English (or the approved 'Shah'/'Imperator'); conlang titles live in ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. The lexicon is a SINGLE FUSED TONGUE (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md), not slash-pairs.

phonology.palette: Old Persian backbone - flowing vowels a i u with long a/i/u, the spirants th(0)/x(kh)/f, sibilants s/sh/z/zh and c(ts), r l, nasals m n, semivowels y v/w, aspirate h, the characteristic endings -a/-ah/-ish/-iya/-ana/-aspa/-arta/-farnah, the ezafe genitive-of-relation '-ahya', heavy-syllable stress - meeting a Latinate Roman substrate: the -us/-um/-a/-ius endings, penultimate stress, c=k, the open Mediterranean syllables and the moderate onset clusters (st-/tr-/pr-/cl-/sp-). Per the CSV: a balanced rhythm with rich vowel length, where the Latin civic roots are smoothed into Persian flowing vowels; grammar SOV, case-inflected with the ezafe construction (the Latin nominal endings absorbed into the Persian relational chain). Theophoric on the Old-Persian-shifted reflexes (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-, Baga-) with Latinate Agrippan construct variants (Tulrius-, Orlandus-, Argentius-).
phonology.phonotactics: CV(C) backbone with the Persian clusters xsh-/sp-/st-/fr-/vr-/thr- and vowel-length distinctive; Latin onset clusters (st-/tr-/pr-/cl-/sp-) admitted and smoothed; Latin -us/-um/-a endings adapted onto Persian flowing -a/-ah/-iya stems; heavy-syllable stress with a Latin penultimate pull; the ezafe '-ahya' relation woven with Latin construct toponyms (Castra-/Via-).

sound_changes: Latin nominal endings adapt to Persian flowing vowels: final -us/-um > -a/-ah, -a retained or lengthened, -ius > -iya, -or > -ar (via > viya, iter > itara, castrum > kastara, forum > fravam); roots take the Persian -a/-ah/-iya inflection

Latin stops and clusters smooth toward the Persian inventory: c always = k, v retained as v/w, geminates simplify (castra > kastara, ferrum > farra), Latin onset clusters st-/tr-/pr-/cl-/sp- admitted but eased onto heavy syllables
Persian heavy-syllable stress imposed on all words with a Latin penultimate pull; the Persian ezafe '-ahya' relation absorbs the Latin construct (X-of-Y = X + -ahya + Y)

retain the Persian spirants th/x/f, the sibilant sh and the ezafe; retain a few Latin signatures - the via/iter road-words, the castra-fort, the legio-host and the lex/ius law-words survive as audible loan-morphs on Persianized stems
very short or consonant-final roots take a Persian -a/-ah ending so the whole tongue flows Persian
fusion_rules.source_tilt: civic/legal/road/material/staple words from Latin roots (the Roman engineering-and-law spine: via-road, castra-fort, urbs-city, forum-market, lex/ius-law, ferrum-iron, argentum-silver, frumen-grain); rule/kin/court/land words from Old Persian roots (the satrapal court and its spine: xshayathiya-king, puthra-son, vith-house, rautah-river, kaufa-mountain, dahyu-land, arta-truth); every root then filtered to one Persian-shaped flowing phonology
portmanteaus: city pura+urbs>puraba (the Persian court-city wedded to the Roman urbs)
fort dida+castra>didakastra (the Persian stronghold and the Roman castrum as one)
road patha+via>pathaviya (the king's-road and the Roman via fused)
law arta+lex>artalexa (right-order and the Roman statute made one word)
temple atashana+templum>atashtempla (the fire-temple and the god-house wedded)
host spada+legio>spadalegia (the Persian war-host and the Roman legion fused)
sacred yazata+sacer>yazasakra (the holy made one word)

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Old-Persian rule/kin/court/land roots + Latinate Roman civic/legal/road/material/staple roots, all run through one Persian-shaped flowing sound-law (Latin -us/-um endings -> -a/-ah/-iya, heavy-syllable stress, ezafe relation); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. NO slash-pairs - this is one tongue.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Persian-descended court keep the filiation 'X-ahya puthra' (son of X) or compact 'X-puthra' and a house (vith-X); the Roman-descended civic stock keep an inherited gens-name woven onto the Persian frame (the gens absorbed as a vith-house); the throne fuses both - a Xshayathiya who also carries a Roman gens and the Persian farnah-glory. Order given-first.
morphology.compounding_rule: Persian quality/relation + element (Arta-xshaca truth-realm, Vahu-farnah good-glory, Baga-data god-given) with the ezafe '-ahya' construct, absorbing the Latin civic compound: the capital Romaria (Roma + the Persian -ya land-suffix), Dida-Xshaca (fort of the realm), Atash-Turvasa (fire of Turvasa) on the Persian frame; resource + feature (Zaranya-kaufa, the gold-mountain); Latin civic compounds Persianized (Castra-Farra > Kastara-Farra, the iron-fort).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a Perso-Roman crown over the wedded east and west: the Shah, the King of Kings, and his vispuhra-kin at the throne, the xshacapavan-satraps over the great provinces, the framatar-governors and the marzapana-wardens beneath; the Roman-descended civic order keeps its forum and its lex beneath the satrapal frame; the magi tend the fire and the pontifices keep the older rites, both serving the crown)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Old Persian native ladder, ascending, beneath an English display ladder (Baron/Marquis/Count/Duke/Prince/[Shah]/[Imperator]). The kingdom-tier DISPLAY ruler is the approved foreign term 'Shah' (the Persian throne-word) and the empire-tier DISPLAY ruler is the approved foreign term 'Imperator' (the Roman imperial style the eastern crown took for itself); all other display tiers are English. Native: Vispati (clan-lord of a vis) barony; Marzapana (march-warden, the marzban) march; Framatar (appointed director/governor) county over a Parada; Xshacapavan (SATRAP, protector of the realm) duchy over a satrapy (Xshacapavanam); Vispuhra (prince of the blood) principality over a great province (Dahyu); Xshayathiya (king; styled the Shah) kingdom over a Xshacam; Xshayathiya Xshayathiyanam (King of Kings; styled the Imperator) empire over the Vispa-Dahyu, all the lands. The Roman-descended civic order keeps its forum-magistracy and its lex beneath the Persian frame. The magu (magus) and the pontifex stand outside the ladder. Rank titles are the real Old-Persian register (allowed); 'Shah' and 'Imperator' are the approved foreign display terms.
title_ladder.heir: Mathishta (the greatest; crown prince) / Visa-puthra (the king's son; the Shah's heir)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler' - here 'Shah' at the kingdom tier and 'Imperator' at the empire tier). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Persian-descended court carry a theophoric or virtue (Arta-/Vahu-) given name + filiation (X-puthra) + a vith-house and a court/satrapal office; the Roman-descended civic stock carry a personal given + an inherited gens woven onto the Persian frame + an earned cognomen; order given-first.
surname_source: theophoric/virtue given (Baga-data = god-given; Arta-xshathra = truth-rule; Turvasa-data)
office (satrap, marzban, framatar) or earned cognomen / honest-deed byname
people_name_convention.dual_register: the satrapal-and-court Persian nobility carry a vith-house, a virtue/theophoric given (Arta-X truth-names, X-farnah glory-names) and an office; the Roman-descended civic stock keep a gens and a cognomen on the Persian frame; the throne fuses both.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Persian-shifted devotional and virtue names: Baga-X (god-X), X-data (X-given), X-farnah (glory-of-X), Vahu-X (good-X), Arta-X (truth-X); Latinate variants on the Agrippan stems woven in (Tulrius-data, Orlandus-farnah). e.g. Turvasa-data, Baga-Urlaspa, Artafarnah, Tulrius-data.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Old-Persian-shifted reflexes PRIMARY (the axsatran shifted stems: Turvasa, Urlaspa, Naumana, Arzanta, Asturna), Latinate Agrippan morphs SECONDARY (the agrippan canon keys: Tulrius, Orlandus, Argentus, Numeno, Realta), recognizably the same powers, never real Iranian/Roman gods. All three alignments (standard lens). The cardinal virtue is ARTA (Truth/Right-order); its opposite is DRAUGA (the Lie). The Persian fire-and-Arta cult is the spine; the Roman temple-rite and the pontifical college are the older western overlay - the crown keeps both the atash fire-altar and the templum god-house.
religion.the_one: Asturna (Latin Aeternus / Itarnu) - the Wise Lord Most High, upholder of Arta and source of the Shah's farnah-glory, honored not petitioned

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Turvasa (Latin Tulrius) - the sun and Arta, lamp of right-order; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Orlandus: Urlaspa (Latin Orlandus) - the iron-oath, war and the cavalier; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Numeno: Naumana (Latin Numeno) - the good mind, wisdom and the law; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Argentus: Arzanta (Latin Argentus) - trade, the road and increase; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Gayanta (Latin Gaiandus) - the enduring earth and mountain
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Riyata (Latin Realta) - the Lady of Waters, mother and mercy

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Asturna the Wise Lord, Turvasa the just, Urlaspa of the sworn war, Riyata the merciful, Naumana of the law - upholding ARTA (Truth/Right-order) and naming the Chaotic powers the hosts of DRAUGA (the Lie), warded; the fire-altar and the law-stele bind alike, and the king's word is bond
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the honest dead and the just kings (kept as fravashi, the honored fore-spirits) and the household and city-spirits; the great powers invoked at the atash fire-altar and the templum situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, the hosts of Drauga the Lie, and names the Lawful powers - and Asturna - as the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers are the hosts of Drauga the Lie, each keeping its shifted morph + a hostile portfolio-epithet: Maraxus -> Marakhsha the Burner-of-Cities (Latin Marahsus the Tyrant-Flame); Vacidus -> Vakida the Devouring-Void (Latin Vacidus the Unmaker); Lusanto -> Lusanta the Coin-Serpent (the Lie made gold).

clergy_ladder.5: Magupati (chief magus of a fire-temple) / Flamana (Roman flamen)
clergy_ladder.9: Magupatan Magupat (the chief of chief magi) / Pontifa Maxima

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Atash ([fire] of [power]) and its fire-temple (Atashana), woven with the Roman Kollegia ([college] of [power]): 'the Atashana of Turvasa', 'the Kollegia of the Dawn Throne'; the magi keep the ever-burning fire (Atar) and the pontifices keep the older templum-rite.
religion.saints_pattern: the honest dead and the just kings, kept as fravashi (fore-spirits) and petitioned at the fire-altar; the deified founders of the western cities (Diva [name], the Roman divus, Persianized); 'the Arta-true [name]' (the righteous [name]).

holy_symbol_motifs.Asturna: a winged ring-disc (the farnah-glory) above a fire-altar and a balance
holy_symbol_motifs.Turvasa: a rayed sun above the upright Arta-measure
holy_symbol_motifs.Urlaspa: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring and the legion-eagle
